title: Levelwise truncations of the adic tower
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension, $A=\mathcal O_E$ its valuation ring, $\varpi$ a uniformizer, and $P_n=A/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $T$ be a scheme, put $B=A_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$ and $R_n=(P_n)_T$, and use the completed-coefficient category $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B))$ and strict tower category of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B))$. Compute its reduction tower $K_\bullet\in D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))$ using one K-flat representative, with level objects $K_n=K\otimes_B^LR_n\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_n))$ and normalization isomorphisms $\rho_n:K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{R_{n+1}}R_n\simeq K_n$ satisfying the quotient cocycle. Here an adic tower, including the relation between its transitions and normalizations, means [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower]. All truncations below are the canonical ones [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category, def-kun-truncations]. Fix $m\in\mathbf Z$.

(1) Use the following explicit Tor-vanishing hypothesis:
$$\operatorname{Tor}^{R_{n+1}}_p(\mathcal H^q(K_{n+1}),R_n)=0
\quad(n\ge1,\ q\ge m+1,\ p\ge1),\tag{TC}$$
where $\operatorname{Tor}^{R}_p(N,S)=\mathcal H^{-p}(N[0]\otimes_R^LS)$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-cohomological-bounds]. Under (TC), the levelwise truncations
$$K_\bullet^-=(\tau^{\le m}K_n)_n,\qquad K_\bullet^+=(\tau^{\ge m+1}K_n)_n$$
are adic towers. Their canonical normalization isomorphisms
$$\tau^{\le m}K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{R_{n+1}}R_n\simeq\tau^{\le m}K_n,
\qquad \tau^{\ge m+1}K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{R_{n+1}}R_n\simeq\tau^{\ge m+1}K_n$$
identify the reduced truncation triangle with the truncation triangle of $K_n$, are natural in maps of reduction towers satisfying (TC), and satisfy the quotient cocycle. A sufficient condition for (TC) is that multiplication by $\varpi$ on $\mathcal H^q(K)$ is injective for every $q\ge m+1$.

Without (TC) the truncated towers need not be adic. For example, if $T$ is nonempty, put $k_T=R_1$ and $K=k_T[-(m+1)]$. Then $\mathcal H^m(K_n)=\mathcal H^{m+1}(K_n)=k_T$ and all other cohomology sheaves vanish, so $\tau^{\le m}K_n\simeq k_T[-m]$. But
$$\mathcal H^{m-p}\bigl((\tau^{\le m}K_{n+1})\otimes^L_{R_{n+1}}R_n\bigr)\simeq k_T\qquad(p\ge0),$$
which precludes normalization. This assertion concerns cohomology; it does not identify $K_n$ with a split sum in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_n))$.

(2) Suppose in addition that $T$ is Noetherian, meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact, and that $K_\bullet$ is uniformly bounded constructible in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower], with local model complexes having zero terms outside one interval $[d_0,d_1]$. Under (TC), both $K_\bullet^-$ and $K_\bullet^+$ are uniformly bounded constructible in that same sense: each admits a finite stratification and common bounded local complexes of adic-lisse finite-type modules with normalization-compatible reductions. The level cohomology of $K_\bullet^-$ is zero outside $[d_0-1,\min(m,d_1)]$ and that of $K_\bullet^+$ is zero outside $[\max(m+1,d_0-1),d_1]$, with an empty interval meaning zero. This asserts existence of common local models, and does not assert that the original model truncations have finite locally free terms or that a raw mapping cone has no terms below $m+1$.

(3) Without (TC), levelwise truncations are still defined as strict-tower derived objects, and for each $n$ their cohomology is $\mathcal H^i(K_n)$ for $i\le m$ (respectively $i\ge m+1$) and zero in the complementary range. These identifications are natural for the strict transition maps. Under (TC) they are also the identifications obtained from the normalized truncation triangles of (1).

If $K_\bullet$ has compatible etale-origin witnesses, namely $L_n\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},P_n)$ and $\alpha_n:\nu_T^*L_n\simeq K_n$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], with isomorphisms $\beta_n:L_{n+1}\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n\simeq L_n$ satisfying the quotient cocycle and $\alpha_n\nu_T^*\beta_n=\rho_n(\alpha_{n+1}\otimes^L R_n)$ under the canonical tensor comparison, then under (TC) the truncated towers have compatible witnesses $\tau^{\le m}L_n$ and $\tau^{\ge m+1}L_n$. Their origin isomorphisms are the truncations of $\alpha_n$ composed with $\nu_T^*\tau\simeq\tau\nu_T^*$, and their normalizations identify the reduced etale truncation triangles with those at level $n$. Here $\nu_T$ is [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and the tensor comparison is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Without (TC), only the levelwise origin isomorphisms and compatibility with strict transition maps are asserted.

proof.text: Apply the levelwise-abelian statement to $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(B)$. Kernels and cokernels in the tower category are the towers of kernels and cokernels. Thus the explicit good truncations, whose only changed term is $\ker d^m$ or $\operatorname{coker}d^m$, evaluate to the good truncations at each level. The same holds before restricting scalars from $R_n$ to $B$, since kernels and cokernels of ring-sheaf modules have their underlying abelian-sheaf kernels and cokernels. The formulas for good-truncation cohomology therefore prove the unconditional cohomology assertions in (3), and functoriality on chain maps gives the truncated strict transitions. These constructions pass to the derived category since the same formulas show that a levelwise quasi-isomorphism stays a levelwise quasi-isomorphism after either truncation. No normalization claim is made in this step.

source.place: Tag 02MZ (lemma-inverse-systems-abelian); Tag 0118 (section-truncations), good truncations and their cohomology

proof.text: Fix $n$ and apply the exact derived scalar extension $F_n=-\otimes^L_{R_{n+1}}R_n$ to the canonical distinguished triangle $X\to K_{n+1}\to Z\to X[1]$, with $X=\tau^{\le m}K_{n+1}$ and $Z=\tau^{\ge m+1}K_{n+1}$. Its middle term identifies with $K_n$ by $\rho_n$. Part (a) of the ring-sheaf cohomological-bounds lemma gives $F_nX\in D^{\le m}$. The cohomology of $Z$ is that of $K_{n+1}$ in degrees $q\ge m+1$ and zero below; (TC) is exactly part (b)'s hypothesis at $a=m+1$, so $F_nZ\in D^{\ge m+1}$. All these are assertions in the quotient-coefficient module categories, rather than an identification of those categories with the completed-coefficient category.

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle), first triangle; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor); blueprint Proof Step 1, tensor the truncation triangle

proof.text: Compare the triangle from step 2 with the canonical truncation triangle $X'\to K_n\to Z'\to X'[1]$. Orthogonality gives $\operatorname{Hom}(F_nX,Z')=0$ and $\operatorname{Hom}((F_nX)[1],Z')=0$, since $F_nX\in D^{\le m}$, $(F_nX)[1]\in D^{\le m-1}$, and $Z'\in D^{\ge m+1}$. The triangle-morphism extension statement therefore supplies a unique morphism of triangles with identity middle component. Reverse the roles of the triangles to obtain its inverse: the composites and the identities have the same middle component and the same uniqueness property. The end components are the required normalization isomorphisms. For any map of the input towers the two composites comparing the corresponding triangles have the same middle component, so uniqueness proves naturality. For three quotient levels, either composite of these triangle comparisons has middle component the original quotient normalization; these coincide by the coefficient datum's quotient cocycle. Uniqueness proves the cocycle for both end components. Their underlying strict transition maps agree with step 1 as follows. After restriction of scalars to $B$, the scalar-extension unit is a morphism from the original triangle to its reduced triangle: on K-flat representatives it is $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, which commutes with differentials, shifts and both summands of a cone, and it descends through the quasi-isomorphisms used to compute derived scalar extension. Compose with the comparison just constructed. Its middle component is the original strict transition by the coefficient datum. Exact restriction of scalars preserves the cohomological bounds, so in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B))$ one has $\operatorname{Hom}(X,Z')=\operatorname{Hom}(X[1],Z')=0$. The triangle-extension statement makes both end components with this middle component unique. Functorially truncating the original strict transition, as in step 1, gives a morphism with that middle component, so its end maps equal the composites of scalar extension with the new normalizations. This proves (1) and its normalized cohomology compatibility in (3).

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9 and Corollaire 1.1.10(ii), pp. 23-24; standard t-structure orthogonality; blueprint Proof Step 1, uniqueness and cocycle

proof.text: For the sufficient condition, the finite free $A$-resolution $[A\xrightarrow{\varpi^a}A]\to P_a$, after the completed constant-sheaf base change, gives $[B\xrightarrow{\varpi^a}B]\to R_a$ for every $a\ge1$. In particular $\varpi^a$ is injective on $B$ and $R_a=B/\varpi^aB$. Tensoring gives the multiplication triangle $K\xrightarrow{\varpi^a}K\to K_a\to K[1]$. Its long exact cohomology sequence yields $0\to\mathcal H^q(K)/\varpi^a\to\mathcal H^q(K_a)\to\mathcal H^{q+1}(K)[\varpi^a]\to0$. Under the sufficient condition the last term is zero for $q\ge m+1$, so $\mathcal H^q(K_{n+1})=M/\varpi^{n+1}M$, where $M=\mathcal H^q(K)$ has injective $\varpi$ action. The free resolution of $R_n$ over $R_{n+1}$ has differentials, starting just before its degree-zero term, $\varpi^n,\varpi,\varpi^n,\varpi,\ldots$. It is exact because $\ker(\varpi^n:R_{n+1}\to R_{n+1})=\varpi R_{n+1}$ and $\ker(\varpi)=\varpi^nR_{n+1}$. It is K-flat by the bounded-above flat-complex lemma. Tensoring it with $M/\varpi^{n+1}M$ is exact in all negative degrees: injectivity of $\varpi$ on $M$ gives respectively $\ker\varpi^n=\varpi M/\varpi^{n+1}M$ and $\ker\varpi=\varpi^nM/\varpi^{n+1}M$. These sheaf equalities can be checked after local lifts along the quotient epimorphism. This computes every higher Tor as zero and proves (TC), without a spectral-sequence convergence assertion or a claim that $B$ is itself a discrete valuation ring.

source.place: Tag 093M (lemma-completion-flat), using Tag 093J (lemma-constant-exact); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YU and bounded-above flat resolutions; blueprint sufficient-condition paragraph, with explicit periodic quotient resolution

proof.text: Assume $T$ is nonempty and take $K=k_T[-(m+1)]$. The same two-term $B$-resolution of $R_n$ gives $K_n$ as $[k_T\xrightarrow{0}k_T][-(m+1)]$ after restricting scalars to $B$. Thus its two nonzero cohomology sheaves are $k_T$ in degrees $m,m+1$. The lower truncation has just one nonzero cohomology sheaf and is therefore $k_T[-m]$ in $D(R_n)$. Compute its next reduction using the periodic free $R_{n+1}$-resolution of $R_n$ from step 4: after tensoring with $k_T$ every differential is zero. Thus $\mathcal H^{m-p}=k_T$ for every $p\ge0$. Here $k_T$ is nonzero: the constant coefficient sections $0$ and $1$ on $T$ remain distinct after every pro-etale covering, since a covering of a nonempty scheme has a nonempty member. Thus the negative-degree cohomology just computed cannot equal that of $k_T[-m]$. On the empty scheme all these sheaves are zero, so this example does not obstruct normalization. The computation does not split the original two-degree object in $D(R_n)$; the two-term $B$-resolution was used only to compute its cohomology. This proves the counterexample and, independently, shows why freeness of terms alone cannot justify (TC).

source.place: Statement (1), torsion counterexample; corrected to assert cohomology rather than an R_n-linear splitting; nonemptiness is necessary for the nonzero coefficient-sheaf counterexample

proof.text: Assume the hypotheses of (2). On a local model domain $U\to T$, let $B_U$ denote the inverse image of $B$, without identifying it with the completed coefficient sheaf formed anew on $U$. The exact pro-etale inverse image, with coefficient ring its own inverse image, pulls the resolution $[B\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}B]\to R_n$ back to $[B_U\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}B_U]\to R_n|_U$. This is a bounded free, hence K-flat, resolution. Tensoring a model $L$ with zero terms outside $[d_0,d_1]$ therefore represents its derived reduction by a complex with zero terms outside $[d_0-1,d_1]$. The same is true of $K_n|_U$ by the model isomorphisms. Restriction to strata and their coverings is exact. Each original level cohomology sheaf is intrinsically constructible: this follows directly from its finite lisse local restrictions on the given finite stratification. By finite-ring constructible-sheaf comparison it is the pullback of an etale constructible sheaf. Local vanishing implies vanishing on its stratum by the sheaf condition for the covering. The pro-etale inverse-image stalk comparison identifies the stalk on a stratum with the original stalk at the image geometric point. Every geometric point of T factors through its unique stratum. The etale/pro-etale comparison-stalk isomorphism therefore makes every geometric stalk of the etale origin zero. Conservativity of the etale geometric points implies that this origin, and hence the original cohomology sheaf, is zero. Thus the original levels, and hence both truncated levels, have a common finite cohomological interval. The sharper intervals displayed in (2) follow by intersecting $[d_0-1,d_1]$ with the surviving truncation range.

source.place: Tag 093M (lemma-completion-flat), the pulled-back two-term quotient resolution; blueprint Proof Step 2, amplitude bookkeeping, with the possible Tor degree d_0-1 retained

proof.text: The original local model reductions have finite lisse cohomology on the common strata. At each level, truncation only retains these cohomology sheaves or replaces them by zero, so each truncated level has intrinsically constructible cohomology, with the same finite stratification, as required in the normalized local-effectivity statement. Step 6 supplies a uniform finite cohomological interval. Steps 2-3 supply the quotient-coefficient level objects and normalized derived reductions inducing the strict transitions and satisfying the cocycle. Finally $T$ is Noetherian by the explicit hypothesis of (2). All hypotheses of normalized constructible local effectivity now hold, separately for $K_\bullet^-$ and $K_\bullet^+$. Its conclusion is exactly the common finite stratification, bounded adic-lisse finite-type local models, and compatible reduction identifications required in (2). It makes no assertion about the terms of the particular raw truncation or raw cone of the original models, which is why the false free-term clause is not used.

proof.text:
Under (TC), the etale upper cohomology sheaves are also $P_n$-acyclic for reduction from $P_{n+1}$. Indeed the derived tensor comparison for the ringed comparison morphism identifies the pullback of each of their higher Tor sheaves with $\operatorname{Tor}^{R_{n+1}}_p(\mathcal H^q(K_{n+1}),R_n)$, using step 8's cohomology comparison and $\alpha_{n+1}$. This is zero by (TC). The sheaf comparison unit is an isomorphism, so $
u_T^*F=0$ implies $F=
u_{T,*}
u_T^*F=0$; hence the etale Tor sheaves vanish. Apply steps 2-3 in the etale module categories to $ eta_n$ to obtain normalization isomorphisms of the truncated etale levels and their cocycles. Pulling the resulting comparison of truncation triangles to the pro-etale site and composing with the truncated $\alpha_n$ gives a comparison whose middle map is $\alpha_n
u_T^* eta_n=ho_n(\alpha_{n+1}\otimes^LR_n)$ by the original compatibility assumption. Step 3's uniqueness therefore gives precisely the two truncated normalization-compatibility equations, not just levelwise origin isomorphisms. The tensor comparisons used here come from the natural balancing map on K-flat representatives: $(x\otimes b)\otimes a\mapsto x\otimes q(b)a$. For three quotients either composition sends a pure tensor to the same product, so the same identifications respect quotient composition. This completes (3).

split_report.summary: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: replaced an undefined cohomology base-change map by explicit sheaf-Tor vanishing; repaired the false quotient-linear split counterexample, cone termwise support and free local model claims. Proved normalization by derived tensor bounds and unique truncation triangle comparison, including cocycles. Uniform constructibility is recovered on Noetherian T by the existing normalized local-effectivity node, using a checked common reduction interval. Made normalized etale-origin compatibility conditional on TC and proved its coherence. One new statement-only general ring-sheaf tensor-bounds node; all other tools reused. Second reading qualifies the counterexample by nonempty T and records independent acyclic-derived-functor searches.
